claim: An external resource counts as part of the thinker only if it is reliably used, directly accessible and trusted on retrieval (Clark and Chalmers coupling conditions). Their automatic-endorsement condition conflicts with safe agent design, which needs verification of notes. New (d06-d10): stale or wrong stored records measurably mislead agents (experience-following, hybrid store stale harm +0.25), and Smart et al. 2025 add two tests for extension: redundancy (does the store add beyond the weights) and agency (does the agent decide when to read).
agent_test: Compare an agent that trusts its notes automatically vs one that re-verifies notes older than N steps, at equal tokens; count stale-note errors.

claim: Epistemic actions (changing the world to simplify thinking) beat internal computation on speed: in Tetris a physical rotation takes about 100 ms vs an estimated 800-1200 ms for mental rotation (3 players only).
agent_test: Give the agent a scratch tool for sub-steps (rotate, tabulate) vs in-head reasoning; compare accuracy per token.

claim: Writing intermediate steps to an external scratchpad raises accuracy on multi-step computation: polynomial evaluation 8.8% to 20.1% (few-shot 137B), program execution 11% to 26.5%. Only one source (Nye 2021) plus the related ReAct and Tree of Thoughts results.
agent_test: Scratchpad on vs off on arithmetic and trace tasks at equal total tokens (scratchpad tokens count).
audit_note: Nye numbers (8.8 to 20.1, 11 to 26.5 with an asterisk for a modified condition) verified; ToT 4% to 74% on Game of 24 confirmed; claim honestly states a single main source.

claim: Tool access lifts LLMs on tasks where the model alone is weak: Toolformer maths 40.4/29.4/44.0 vs 14.8/6.3/15.0 with tools disabled; calculator used on 97.9% of math items; gap persists at 1.6B parameters.
agent_test: Calculator or code interpreter on vs off for numeric items; log tool-use rate.

claim: Interleaving reasoning with environment actions cuts hallucinated facts but ReAct alone is not better than chain-of-thought on HotpotQA (ReAct 27.4 EM vs CoT 29.4 vs CoT-SC 33.4). Combining ReAct with CoT-SC gives the best result (35.1). Gap search: at matched tokens on Qwen3-8B math, a pruned tool loop roughly ties self-consistency (AIME25 60.9 vs 56.7, AIME24 72.7 vs 73.3); no modern ReAct-vs-SC matched test found.
agent_test: ReAct vs CoT vs CoT-SC vs hybrid at equal tokens on multi-hop QA.

claim: ReAct fails differently from CoT: CoT failures are 56% hallucination, ReAct 0%; ReAct failures are 47% reasoning error (often repeated steps) and 23% empty or useless search.
agent_test: Add a repeat-action detector; measure rate of repeated thought-action pairs and accuracy.

claim: An action-observation loop beats act-only prompting in embodied and web tasks: ALFWorld best ReAct 71% vs Act 45% vs BUTLER 37%; mean relative gain over Act 62%; WebShop 40.0 vs 30.1.
agent_test: Thought steps on vs off in a tool environment at equal action budget.

claim: Paging memory in and out under model control greatly improves long-context retrieval: MemGPT deep memory retrieval GPT-4 32.1% to 92.5%, GPT-3.5 38.7% to 66.9%; nested key-value lookup collapses to 0% for fixed context while MemGPT with GPT-4 holds. Authors own benchmark. Gap search: no clean independent replication; rival-author tables put Letta near full-context level on LoCoMo (74.0 vs 72.9, unverified).
agent_test: Fixed-context baseline vs paged memory with search tool on long-history tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Reflection written to external memory helps: Reflexion adds 8% absolute over episodic memory alone; HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80.1%.
agent_test: Retry loop with verbal reflection vs raw retry at equal tokens.

claim: A growing external skill or experience library sustains progress: Voyager got 63 unique items, 3.3x the best baseline, and plateaus without the skill library; generative-agent memory, reflection and planning each raise believability (TrueSkill 29.89 full vs 21.21 none).
agent_test: Ablate a persistent library of solved sub-procedures across tasks at equal tokens.
audit_note: Voyager 63 items 3.3x counterparts and plateau without skill library, and Generative Agents TrueSkill 29.89 vs 21.21 verified; Voyager entries b20/c11/c12 are one paper.

claim: Interface design of the tool matters as much as tool presence: SWE-agent purpose-built interface solved 10.7 points more of 300 SWE-bench Lite items than a default shell agent; linting guardrails and concise feedback help.
agent_test: Same model, raw tool output vs trimmed and linted tool output.
audit_note: SWE-agent paper states 10.7 points over a default shell agent on 300 SWE-bench Lite items and linting/concise-feedback ablations; 'matters as much as tool presence' is the researcher's interpretation.

claim: Position in context changes how well stored information is used: a relevant passage in the middle drops GPT-3.5 multi-document QA by over 20 points, below its closed-book 56.1%.
agent_test: Put the key note first or last vs middle; use retrieval to re-surface it.

claim: Active agent-managed memory got more reuse than passive RAG in one test: 54.5-58.6% reuse vs 0% and 17-18% net efficiency after 3.3x more operations. The reported Cohen d of 195.66 comes from a tiny test (8 documents, t(18)); treat as unreliable.
agent_test: Replicate on real tasks with a proper baseline and tokens counted.

claim: Memory architectures beat plain long context in their own papers: Extended Mind Transformers 70B+RAG 59.34% vs GPT-4 52.28% at 2k; EMT 7B holds 33.54% at 16k vs plain chat Llama2 17.68%; A-Mem uses about 1,200 tokens per operation vs 16,900 for full context.
agent_test: Retrieval memory vs full context at matched tokens.
audit_note: All numbers verified; note EMT 7B actually trails plain Chat Llama2 at 2k and 4k (38.59 vs 42.74, 37.95 vs 41.96) and wins only at 8k and 16k, and A-Mem's 16,900-token baseline is LoCoMo/MemGPT.

claim: The Google effect on memory (people recall less of what they expect to look up) is contested: Sparrow 2011 Exp 2 recall 0.31 (erase) vs 0.22 (save), but the Camerer 2018 replication failed (pooled p=.4493) and a 2020 Stroop replication found no conclusive evidence. A 2024 meta-analysis reports d=0.39 to 0.91 for some outcomes but ns for cognitive measurement.
schema_part: G (do not assume offloading is free)
agent_test: Do not copy the human result; measure agent recall of facts it knows it can look up.

claim: The brain-drain effect (mere presence of a phone lowers capacity) is not supported overall. Hartanto 2024 (4,368 participants, 33 studies): d=-0.02, 95% CI [-0.06,0.01]; only OSPAN shows d=-0.13 and it is publication-biased (bias-adjusted d=-0.04). Boettger 2023 (22 studies, use plus presence): g=-0.14, memory g=-0.23. Two direct replications failed.
agent_test: Not testable on an agent; skip.

claim: Offloading is guided by confidence and heavy offloading carries a cost: reminders raised hit rate 82.7% to 88.1% (Boldt and Gilbert); LLM-assisted essay writers failed to quote their own essay 83.3% (15/18) vs 11.1% in controls (small study, methodological criticism published).
agent_test: Measure agent accuracy on questions about its own prior output with notes hidden.

claim: AI help can reduce skill gain in humans: Shen and Tamkin d=0.738 lower quiz (n=52); delegation style about 39% vs conceptual inquiry about 65%. A larger test (N=704) found no significant unaided deficit (0.65 vs 0.62, OR 0.80, p=.244) but offloading predicted worse test items. Bastani 2025 PNAS field experiment (nearly 1,000 students): unrestricted GPT tutor +48% in practice but -17% on exam vs control; guardrailed tutor +127% practice, exam equal to control (secondary summary read).
schema_part: G/O (use tool to check, not to replace)
agent_test: Not a thinking-quality claim for the agent; use as a design caution for any human-facing mode.

claim: Philosophical case that LLM plus retrieval is an extended system (Smart, Clowes and Clark 2025) was opened: it is qualitative (gpt-3.5, first responses, no scores), and itself names a redundancy problem (GPTMODIFIED without retrieval already knew wideware and Otto) and an agency problem (the app, not the LLM, calls the store).
agent_test: None; conceptual.

claim: Critiques of extended mind (Adams and Aizawa; Rupert) and systems views (Hutchins, Wegner) were listed but not opened, so no claim is made about them. Gap search: transactive-memory style sharing exists for LLMs (MATM, d16) but no numeric Wegner or Hutchins result was opened.
agent_test: None.

claim: A persistent external store helps tool-using agents only if it overwrites rather than accumulates. MERIT (23,440 episodes): no memory 0.00 on dependent tasks; hard-tier success retrieval 0.35-0.70, fact store 0.75-1.00, summary 0.70-1.00, hybrid 0.50-0.80; implementation swap moved success up to 60 points; stale-memory harm hybrid +0.25.
agent_test: Notes file with timestamps, overwrite-on-update vs append-only, with injected stale items; count wrong actions.

claim: Verify before writing to memory. Adding every run to memory flattens or lowers agent success (error propagation, agents copy similar stored runs closely); strict evaluator-gated addition keeps improving and in one agent passed the ground-truth-retrieval variant after about 2,000 runs.
agent_test: Write-gate (checker or tests pass) vs write-all; track success over a stream of tasks.

claim: On LoCoMo, a Mem0-style fact memory scored 57.68 vs 92.85 for full long context with GPT-5-mini (Pollertlam et al.), but in a separate study (Terranova et al.) memory methods using over 90% fewer tokens were competitive with or better than full context for some models (GPT-4o-mini A-Mem average-F1 rank 1.80 vs 3.40 for full context) and much better on adversarial questions (77.64 vs 52.94); Pollertlam et al. find memory cheaper after about 10 turns at 100k context.
agent_test: Raw log plus short notes vs full context on tasks with unanswerable items; report tokens.
audit_note: Numbers verified, but Terranova et al. report memory methods are competitive or superior to full context on LoCoMo (GPT-4o-mini A-Mem average F1 rank 1.80 vs full context 3.40; Qwen too), so 'do not beat full context on factual recall' holds only for the Mem0 system in Pollertlam et al. and for Llama; the 90% token saving is from Terranova's A-Mem, not Mem0.
claim_before_audit: When the history fits in context, extracted notes do not beat full context on factual recall: LoCoMo accuracy memory 57.68 vs long-context 92.85 (GPT-5-mini). But memory uses over 90% fewer tokens, is cheaper after about 10 turns at 100k context, and is better on unanswerable questions (GPT-4o-mini adversarial 77.64 A-Mem vs 52.94 full).

claim: Repeated identical tool calls are common (29.0% of CodeGym tasks with full history, 57.3% under compression for Qwen3-8B) and looping runs fail more (59.5% vs 33.4%). A visible action log cuts repeats (3.3% vs 48.8% without the record) but an exact-duplicate blocker leaves proposals unchanged (71.3% vs 69.8%).
agent_test: Action log plus duplicate blocker plus forced alternative vs none; measure repeat rate and tokens.

claim: Smart et al. 2025 imply two testable conditions for counting a store as extending an LLM: it must add information not already in the weights (ablate the store), and the agent must itself decide when to consult it. Neither has been scored numerically.
agent_test: Run with and without the store on facts the model does and does not know; compare.

claim: Shared trajectory stores across agents help modestly and only when retrieval is task-matched: MATM ALFWorld 47% to 55% (64.3% with reranker), WebArena 18% to 20%; unmatched full-index retrieval 0.298 vs task-type-matched 0.599.
agent_test: Index notes or past solutions by task type and compare to a flat index.
